source_snapshot.test_name_items: Upgrade / Downgrade FPGA firmware by Redfish when system is off
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Upgrade / Downgrade FPGA firmware through redfish.
1. Enter the command on the command line to set the behavior of BMC after update.
Command : curl -k -X PATCH https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/ -H "Content-Type:application/json" -d '{"HttpPushUriOptions":{"HttpPushUriApplyTime":{"ApplyTime": "Immediate"}}}'
2. Change the name of the firmware file to be updated in the green text. This command may take some time to upload the firmware to BMC.
Command : curl -k -X POST https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/update -H "Content-Type:application/octet-stream" --data-binary @${File_name}
3. Waiting for the flash progress complete.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
Firmware should be flashed successfully after BMC reset only one time.
curl -k -X GET https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: curl (Redfish REST client, on the BMC side) + FPGA image (user provides)
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: DeepSeek narrows the two-direction case to FPGA downgrade and proposes the source-style PATCH/POST, assumed TaskService polling and FirmwareInventory check while the host is off.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: PATCH/POST responses, TaskService transcript, final FirmwareInventory and clean host power-on.
deepseek_columns.risk: DeepSeek identifies the destructive FPGA write and interruption risk.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL; keeps FPGA, host-off and Redfish scope, but omits the upgrade direction and assumes generic endpoint/task semantics without validating component binding or secure transport.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: BLOCKED / CHANGED; correctly flags credentials, TLS, reset and recovery, but treats obtainable vendor/project inputs as permanent semantic failure.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 729/2291 preserves the literal source commands, FPGA target and one-BMC-reset criterion.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: The archived sequence-898 record classified the destructive update FULLY AUTOMATABLE; it is non-counting history and not reused as a decision.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-34 permits approved tool binding with coverage accounting; ED-36 makes images and parameters readiness; ED-38 keeps verdict ownership with engineers; the approved target rule retains FPGA exactly.

original_test_intent: Run approved FPGA upgrade and downgrade through Redfish while the host is off, allow exactly one BMC reset as the source acceptance boundary, and prove the intended FPGA member becomes active without loss of BMC or later host health.
original_method: The Master row PATCHes Immediate apply behavior, POSTs a binary image to a fixed update URI, waits for unspecified completion and GETs FirmwareInventory after one BMC reset. Embedded default credentials and `curl -k` are preserved as unsafe source text, not recommended execution.
manual_activity: An engineer must approve the exact FPGA/image/direction, vendor Redfish action, one-BMC-reset activation semantics and recovery immediately before each write. The API and evidence flow may then be automated, but destructive approval and the final verdict remain human-owned.
required_inputs: FPGA device/board revision, current version and approved upgrade/downgrade versions
signed FPGA images, hashes, release notes and transition order
advertised component-bound Redfish action, payload, apply-time and task/terminal-response contract
protected credentials, trusted management CA and validated FPGA inventory mapping
host-off/BMC-standby, exactly-one-reset, post-reset health and recovery plan
safety_requirements: Never execute the literal credential-in-URL commands or `curl -k`; authenticate the identified BMC through approved secret handling and verified TLS.
Discover a vendor-approved action and a selector or inventory member that uniquely binds the image to the FPGA; generic UpdateService success may target the wrong component.
Confirm the source's one-BMC-reset rule, including initiator, timing and FPGA activation effect; do not silently substitute an AC cycle or host reboot.
Submit one approved direction at a time and correlate only its returned task or terminal response; never retry, reverse direction or add a reset after uncertainty.
Keep BMC standby power stable and preserve HTTP/task/reset, SEL and console evidence for recovery.
agent_execution_scope: Perform read-only service, component inventory, host-state, BMC health and task discovery; validate the signed image and obtain explicit approval.
After approval, submit only the component-bound vendor action, monitor its exact completion and the single BMC reset, then verify the mapped FPGA member and BMC recovery.
Collect later host POST/OS evidence if required by the project and report raw results without setting PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED.
engineer_actions: Approve device/image/order, secure vendor action, one-reset activation behavior and recovery for each direction.
Confirm that the exact FPGA member activated after one BMC reset and issue direction-specific verdicts.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its staged lifecycle broadly fits, but it covers downgrade only, inherits unsafe authentication/TLS, assumes `/update` and TaskService, and never proves FirmwareInventory maps to the intended FPGA.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the platform-advertised component-bound Redfish updater with protected authentication, trusted TLS, signed-image binding, response-correlated completion and the approved single BMC reset.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: FPGA target, source PATCH/POST/GET, Immediate setting, host-off condition, one-BMC-reset criterion, linked script and 10/30-minute values remain immutable source evidence.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Map the exact FPGA to its advertised inventory/update target, submit one approved signed image, monitor the returned completion object, observe exactly one approved BMC reset, and independently verify FPGA activation plus BMC/host health.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only BMC/FPGA combinations exposing an approved FPGA update action and unambiguous inventory mapping.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record FPGA/board image, BMC, Redfish schema/service, client, CA and recovery-tool versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor Redfish FPGA update, BMC-reset activation and recovery documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Removes exposed credentials, TLS bypass and assumed endpoint/task behavior while adding explicit FPGA member binding and reset correlation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Another approved tool may demonstrate a project FPGA transition but cannot claim this Redfish path; a generic inventory string cannot prove the correct FPGA instance or full platform recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: If the FPGA is not uniquely represented in FirmwareInventory, independent vendor readback is mandatory.

project_override_considerations: Project SPEC may authorize a different tool, but must record original Redfish versus actual method, reason, engineer approval, checkpoint equivalence and unverified Redfish coverage. FPGA must not be silently replaced by CPLD, and missing artifacts remain readiness inputs.
expected_evidence: approved FPGA device/board/version/image matrix with hashes and signatures
redacted authenticated request/response and exact correlated completion transcript
one-BMC-reset initiator/timeline and restored management reachability
pre/post authoritative FPGA identity/version plus validated FirmwareInventory mapping
BMC/SEL and required host POST/OS health, recovery readiness and separate engineer verdicts

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently target FPGA through Redfish with the host off and exactly one BMC reset. The unsafe literals and incomplete vendor bindings are method defects/readiness gaps, not competing purposes; no AC-cycle requirement is imported from the adjacent WebUI row.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The FPGA target, two version directions, Redfish method and one-reset boundary are identifiable. Vendor action semantics, images, secure access, member mapping and recovery can be supplied as named inputs, so the case is confirmation-gated rather than permanently blocked.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keeps its PARTIAL-equivalent package/approval class, restores upgrade coverage, and adds required component binding, secure transport, exact completion and reset correlation.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains the security and recovery gates but removes permanent BLOCKED because the missing contracts are obtainable without redefining FPGA or Redfish coverage.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Rejects FULLY AUTOMATABLE because firmware images and destructive confirmation are mandatory even when all runtime interfaces are programmable.

review_improvement: Prevents a generic UpdateService response or FirmwareInventory entry from proving the wrong programmable device and makes the source's single BMC reset auditable without borrowing AC-cycle semantics.
independent_technical_reasoning: The state machine is scriptable only after the project proves which inventory/update target is the FPGA and how one BMC reset activates it. Those are resolvable vendor/project bindings, so BLOCKED is too strong. Because a signed image and explicit destructive approval are mandatory, FULLY AUTOMATABLE is also incorrect; REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION preserves both capability and safety.
